Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

word noun

promise

also give one’s word, keep one’s word, break one’s word, you have my word, a promise, keep a promise, break a promise, fulfil a promise, fulfill a promise, word of honour

classical

Cic. Off. 1.39: fidem hostī datam fallere
Cic. Off. 1.23: fundāmentum autem est jūstitiae fidēs
Traupman 111: fidem dare (frangere, servāre)
Traupman 159, 408

fidēs, fideī f.

noun, fifth declension

one’s word, pledge, good faith

Fidem dare, to give one’s word (Cic. Rab. Perd. 28); fidem servāre, to keep it (Caes. BG 6.36); fidem fallere or frangere, to break it (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • prōmissum, prōmissī n. — a promise

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 106: prōmissa servāre; M-O s.v. promise, keep a; Cic. Off. 3.92: pacta et prōmissa servāre (Lewis & Short s.v. prōmittō); Traupman 106: to keep promises; to break promises, prōmissa servāre; prōmissa frangere

    Prōmissa servāre, to keep one’s promises (Cic., in Morgan–Owens).

  • fidem servāre — to keep one’s word

    also used · classical · Caes. BG 6.36 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 147, 159, 408

  • fidem fallere — to break one’s word

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.39 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 159

    Cicero has fidem datam fallere.

  • fidem dare — to give one’s word

    also used · classical · Cic. Rab. Perd. 28 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 159, 408

  • verba dare — cheat, deceive

    avoid · classical · Ter. And. 211: Cui verba dare difficile est.; Cic. Att. 15.16a (Lewis & Short)

    A false friend: verba dare alicui is to fob someone off with words, to cheat him (Lewis & Short), not to give one’s word.

Examples

  • ad supplicium redīre māluit quam fidem hostī datam fallere

    he chose to go back to be put to death rather than break the word he had given the enemyCic. Off. 1.39

  • fundāmentum autem est jūstitiae fidēs, id est dictōrum conventōrumque cōnstantia et vēritās

    and the foundation of justice is good faith: that is, standing by what has been said and agreed, and being true to itCic. Off. 1.23

  • fidem frangere

    to break one’s wordTraupman 408

See also word, promise.
